prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1318; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left-turn lane at an intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, when the collision occurred. Driver 1 stated that the vehicle was turning left when it was struck by Driver 2, who was proceeding through the intersection. Driver 2 gave a statement consistent with this account, and independent witnesses at the scene described the sequence of events in the same way. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front driver-side area of Driver 1's vehicle, which is consistent with the reported angle and force of impact. Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision and was present at the scene when officers arrived. Driver 1 reported neck and back pain following the crash, and the reported symptoms are consistent with the type and force of the impact observed. Officers found no indication of prior damage to the vehicle. Driver 1 was identified as the named driver on the insurance policy for the vehicle involved.
